focus: A11 cli-opencode dispatch to both versions: version detection for two --version formats, the full v1->v2 flag and subcommand matrix, the cli-opencode files encoding v1-only behaviour, and the deep-loop runner's opencode command builder
answeredQuestions: How should cli-opencode detect the installed version and dispatch to v1 and v2, with a full flag and subcommand matrix?

graphEvents.label: version string formats differ and the ^1. guard fails on v2
deep-loop runtime has no semver signal and hardcodes command -v opencode
v2 --command replacement is the session.command API operation
nine subcommand renames and seven v2-only additions

label: v2 run lists only twelve FLAGS and deletes seven the repo depends on: --variant (effort folds into --model provider/model#variant), --command, --dir (relocated to a positional directory), --pure, --share, --attach (replaced by --server) and --port (relocated to serve --port); it also changes -f/--file from array to string, widens -s/--session to create-or-continue, drops the --fork precondition and replaces the --log-level choice set with all|trace|debug|info|warn|warning|error|fatal|none. There is therefore no v1-and-v2-safe invocation line: the v1 form fails on v2 with unknown flags and a naive --dir-dropped form silently runs in the wrong cwd.

Version detection: opencode --version prints 1.19.3 (bare semver) while opencode2 --version prints 'opencode v2.0.32' (product word, space, v prefix). A parser must accept ^\s*(?:[A-Za-z][\w.-]*\s+)?[vV]?(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:[-+][\w.-]+)?\s*$ and branch on the major. The repo's existing guard at SKILL.md:134 is 'opencode --version | grep -q ^1\.', which fails on a healthy v2 install and reports version drift, while the SKILL.md:133 pin to v1.3.17 is already stale against the observed 1.19.3.

The deep-loop runtime never learns an opencode version. resolveExecutableVersion (fanout-run.cjs:2093) does not spawn --version; it realpaths the PATH entry, stats it and returns sha256:<digest> of the binary contents (line 2108) — a strong identity primitive but not a semver, so no code path can compare a major. isOpencodeBinaryAvailable (fanout-run.cjs:2962) hardcodes 'command -v opencode', so a machine with only opencode2 is reported as having no executor, and the dispatch table at fanout-run.cjs:2923 maps cli-opencode to its builder with no version input. Minimal addition: resolveExecutableSemver reusing the existing ${realpath}:${size}:${mtimeMs} cache key.

The v2 replacement for 'run --command' is the documented OpenAPI operation POST /api/session/{sessionID}/command (operationId session.command) taking {name, text, files, agents, skills, delivery}; the near-twin session.prompt takes {id, text, files, agents, skills, metadata, delivery, resume} with no 'name', so it is the plain-message path and not a command path. opencode api <operation|method path> with --data/--header/--param makes both reachable from the CLI without curl. session.create also accepts {id, parentID, title, agent, model, location, metadata, permissions} and session.switchModel takes {model}, so v2 can set agent and model on the session instead of on the invocation.

Subcommand tree v1 to v2: export[ID] and import<file> move under session; attach is replaced by --server/--standalone; agent create|list is gone (listing via 'debug agents' or GET /api/agent); the providers alias disappears leaving auth; models loses its positional provider; web becomes serve (v2 serve = API plus web server) and serve's flags become --hostname/--port/--cors(repeatable)/--service/--stdio; completion becomes the --completions flag; plugin <module> becomes plugin <subcommand>; db, github and pr have no counterpart. v2 adds api, service, reload, pair, mini, uninstall and upgrade|update.

--dangerously-skip-permissions appears in neither captured run help page (a grep for 'dangerously' across the whole capture directory returns nothing) although SKILL.md:231 and fanout-run.cjs:2341 both depend on it. Help text cannot distinguish a hidden flag from an absent one, so its presence on 1.19.3 and 2.0.32 is UNKNOWN; the documented --auto is present on both and is functionally equivalent.

The cli-opencode change surface is concentrated in four places plus the playbook: SKILL.md lines 5,133,134,153,157,159,165,171,189,203,207,215,219,249; references/cli-reference.md lines 3,18,46,61 and the flag table at 103-119 plus 123,132,142,163,165,167; references/providers-and-models.md lines 17,113,119,131,133 where --variant is the effort lever throughout; hard-rules.json where three of five rules are v1-shaped (command-flag-for-slash-prompt, share-requires-confirmation, no-bare-agent-general) while stdin-redirect-required and explicit-model-required stay universal; assets/prompt-templates.md lines 76,78,112,116,157,159 with six rendered --variant invocations; and 20 manual-testing-playbook files that name the v1 flag set.

The migration-safe intersection both versions honour is: --version/-v, --format default|json with identical choices, --agent, --title, --thinking, --auto, -c/--continue, -s/--session, --fork, -f/--file, --print-logs. Everything else in the cli-opencode documented surface is branch-only. A shared detection helper should resolve the binary from $OPENCODE_BIN, then opencode2, then opencode, parse either version format, map major 1 to v1 and >=2 to v2, refuse to dispatch on an unparsable version rather than guess, and optionally confirm capability with 'run --help | grep -- --variant' because capability is what dispatch needs, not the version number.
Every documented cli-opencode invocation must be resolved through a detected major before rendering; a single invocation line cannot serve both 1.19.x and 2.0.x because seven run flags diverge.
Binary resolution and version resolution are two separate steps: opencode2 is a distinct binary name, so no version parser reachable only through an 'opencode'-named path can find it.

direction: Replace run --command on v2 with a bare '/family:name args' run message
reason: Iteration 7 established that v1 delivers slash text as raw prose and nothing captured for v2 shows run-level expansion; the documented v2 route is POST /api/session/{id}/command (session.command), whose body has an explicit name field that session.prompt lacks.

direction: Detect the version from the sha256 identity the runtime already computes
reason: resolveExecutableVersion returns a content digest by design (fanout-run.cjs:2093-2114), which detects a binary swap but carries no ordering, so it cannot answer 'is this major 1 or 2'. A semver resolve is required in addition.
